version.changelog:
- Updated version to 0.6.3 with revised documentation for improved clarity.
- Repository and author links now point to https://gitee.com/random_player/cmic-skill-scanner.
- Added a "permissions" section, listing required and non-required permissions.
- Reformatted binary information, usage instructions, and malware detection details for better readability.
- Updated links to releases, source, and checksum files.

llm.summary: The skill mostly describes a local skill-scanner (which fits its name) but contains several internal contradictions (a claimed bundled binary that is not present, contradictory statements about reading system files and network activity, and upload/bridge options) that merit caution before running anything.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose (local scanner for skills) is plausible and many instructions align, but the SKILL.md claims a bundled binary at assets/bin/skillscan (with checksums and release URLs) while the package manifest does not include that binary. That mismatch is unexpected: either the package is incomplete, or users are expected to obtain the binary from the external repository. Both possibilities change the trust model and are not justified in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md declares the scanner 'does NOT read arbitrary system files, access credentials, or make network calls' while other parts of the documents contradict that: the 'What It Detects' table explicitly references reading ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, and config locations to detect credential theft, and INSTALL.md documents an --upload-url option and an external engine bridge. These contradictions leave unclear what files may actually be read and whether network exfiltration is possible.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec (instruction-only skill), which is low risk in itself, but SKILL.md/INSTALL.md repeatedly reference running a bundled binary and verifying a SHA-256. The package manifest does not include the binary file that SKILL.md claims is present. That inconsistency raises the risk that a user or agent may be directed to fetch and run a binary from the external Gitee releases page — downloading and executing an external binary has high risk unless the user independently verifies it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials (which is appropriate), but the documentation lists credential file paths as detection targets (e.g., ~/.ssh, ~/.aws). The SKILL.md metadata lists only 'local-file-read' permission, but the docs are ambiguous about whether the scanner will access sensitive home-directory files. Also the optional upload/bridge flags permit transmitting scan results (which may include scanned file contents) to external URLs — this capability is not reflected in required permissions or metadata and increases sensitivity.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not declare system-wide changes, and has no declared install hooks. Autonomy (model invocation) is allowed by default but that is the platform norm. There is no evidence the skill requests persistent elevated privileges or modifies other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not run any binary from this package until you verify what binary will be executed and where it came from. Concrete steps: (1) Confirm whether assets/bin/skillscan is actually included in the package — if missing, do not attempt to fetch or run a binary from the Internet without review. (2) If a binary is present, compute its sha256 locally and compare it to the published checksum and the release page before executing. (3) Inspect the upstream Gitee repository and release artifacts (or preferably build from source) so you can audit what the binary does. (4) Be cautious with the --upload-url or --engine external options: they can transmit report contents (which may contain scanned files) to external servers; only use them with a trusted destination. (5) If you need to run the scanner, do so in an isolated environment (sandbox or VM) and confirm whether it will read sensitive home files (~/.ssh, ~/.aws); if so, avoid exposing those directories or provide a sanitized copy of the skill to scan. If you cannot verify the binary/source, treat this package as untrusted.
